answer:
The “Papers of individual botanists” series (MSS Sherard 26‑448) contains papers from a number of 17th‑ and 18th‑century botanists.  
From that series, the botanists whose papers appear **do not include a Sherardian Professor of Botany** (i.e. they were never appointed to the chair). In the order in which their manuscripts are arranged in the Sherardian Library, those botanists are:

1. **Robert Morison**  
   – Papers of Robert Morison are listed in the series (MSS Sherard 26‑8)【4†L4-L7】【4†L21-L24】.  
   – Morison was never a Sherardian Professor.  

2. **John Bobart**  
   – Papers of John Bobart appear in the collection (MSS Sherard 26‑17)【4†L5-L8】【4†L29-L32】.  
   – Bobart never held the Sherardian chair.  

3. **William Sherard**  
   – W. Sherard’s own papers are part of the series (MSS Sherard 26‑26/28)【4†L10-L13】【4†L36-L38】.  
   – Although the chair was named after him, Sherard himself never occupied the Sherardian Professorship.  

No other botanists with papers in the MSS Sherard 26‑448 series were ever appointed Sherardian Professor of Botany; the list of holders of the chair (Dillenius, Supersub,…,Østergaard) excludes these three.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Professorship in the University of Oxford

The **Sherardian Chair of Botany** is a professorship at the [University of Oxford] that was established in 1734.[[1]] It was created following an [endowment] by [William Sherard] on his death in 1728. In his will, Sherard stipulated that the first holder of the chair was to be [Johann Jacob Dillenius].[[2]] The Sherardian Professor is also a [fellow] "Fellow (college)") of [Magdalen College, Oxford]

## List of Sherardian Professors of Botany

[[edit]]

* [Johann Jacob Dillenius] (1734 to 1747)
* [Humphry Sibthorp] "Humphry Sibthorp (botanist)") (1747 to 1783)
* [John Sibthorp] (1784 to 1796)
* [George Williams] "George Williams (physician)") (1796 to 1834)[[3]]
* [Charles Giles Bridle Daubeny] (1834 to 1867)[[4]]
* [Marmaduke Alexander Lawson] (1868 to 1882)[[5]]
* [Isaac Bayley Balfour] (1884 to 1888)
* [Sydney Howard Vines] (1888 to 1919)
* [Frederick Keeble] (1920 to 1927)
* [Arthur Tansley] (1927 to 1937)
* [Theodore Osborn] (1937 to 1953)
* [C. D. Darlington] (1953 to 1971)
* [F. R. Whatley] (1971 to 1991)
* Hugh G. Dickinson (1991 to 2009)[[1]]
* [Liam Dolan] (2009 to 2021)[[6]]
* Lars Østergaard (2022 to present)[[7]]

The “Papers of individual botanists” series (MSS Sherard 26‑448) contains papers from a number of 17th‑ and 18th‑century botanists.  
From that series, the botanists whose papers appear **do not include a Sherardian Professor of Botany** (i.e. they were never appointed to the chair). In the order in which their manuscripts are arranged in the Sherardian Library, those botanists are:

1. **Robert Morison**  
   – Papers of Robert Morison are listed in the series (MSS Sherard 26‑8)【4†L4-L7】【4†L21-L24】.  
   – Morison was never a Sherardian Professor.  

2. **John Bobart**  
   – Papers of John Bobart appear in the collection (MSS Sherard 26‑17)【4†L5-L8】【4†L29-L32】.  
   – Bobart never held the Sherardian chair.  

3. **William Sherard**  
   – W. Sherard’s own papers are part of the series (MSS Sherard 26‑26/28)【4†L10-L13】【4†L36-L38】.  
   – Although the chair was named after him, Sherard himself never occupied the Sherardian Professorship.  

No other botanists with papers in the MSS Sherard 26‑448 series were ever appointed Sherardian Professor of Botany; the list of holders of the chair (Dillenius, Supersub,…,Østergaard) excludes these three.
